subject: Gilbert et al. (2009)
object: Gilbert et al. (2009) reported a large multigenerational Ohio kindred with a highly penetrant autosomal dominant neurologic disorder causing spasticity and dystonia. Spasticity and weakness began anywhere from the first year of life to the sixth decade, and dystonia began between the first and third decades. Affected members had no ataxia and no apparent cognitive involvement. Neuroimaging and peripheral neurophysiology were normal.

subject: Gilbert et al. (2009)
object: Gilbert et al. (2009) reported that generalized dystonia improved markedly with deep brain stimulation in 1 affected child from the kindred.

subject: Gilbert et al. (2009)
object: Gilbert et al. (2009) used single-point and multipoint linkage analysis with microsatellite markers and SNP array genotyping to map the disease locus in the Ohio kindred to chromosome 2q24-q31. The region was flanked by rs1424937 and rs1559510, lay proximal to SPG13, and contained no known HSP or dystonia genes. A secondary analysis looking for candidate regions segregating with the dystonia phenotype found two regions with parametric lod scores above 2.0.

subject: Gilbert et al. (2009)
object: Based on the clinical presentation and the linkage results, Gilbert et al. (2009) concluded that this disease is a novel neurologic disorder, distinct from known forms of hereditary spastic paraplegia and dystonia.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) summarized a large, multigenerational family (Family-1) segregating autosomal dominant dystonia and/or spastic paraplegia. Of 40 individuals in the pedigree, 18 were affected with either childhood-onset, progressive generalized dystonia or adult-onset, gradually progressive spastic paraplegia. Less severe, later-onset focal limb and neck dystonia and spasmodic dysphonia also occurred. Brain MRI and peripheral nerve physiology were normal when performed.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) reported that the Family-1 proband had unilateral upper limb dystonia onset at age 2 years that generalized to the trunk and all limbs, causing loss of ambulation. His father and grandfather had the hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotype, with progressive leg weakness and spasticity beginning after age 20 years. Metabolic studies, including blood lactate and pyruvate, serum amino acids, urine organic acids, and acylcarnitine profiles, were normal in the proband and his father.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) reported that bilateral pallidal deep brain stimulation, implanted at age 9 years in the Family-1 proband, restored ambulation and limb use, and the response remained excellent at age 25 years.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: In affected members of Family-1, a family whose disorder had previously been mapped to chromosome 2q24-q31, Neilson et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing restricted to the linkage region to identify a heterozygous missense variant in the ATP5MC3 gene (c.318C>G, p.Asn106Lys). Sanger sequencing showed that only affected individuals carried the variant. The variant was absent from gnomAD v2.1.1 and v3.1.1, affects a highly conserved loop that contacts the F1 subunit, and was predicted damaging by all in silico tools used. The authors concluded that ATP5MC3 remains the primary candidate for the spastic paraplegia in this family.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) described a right-handed boy (Family-2) of European descent, born to healthy unrelated parents with no family history of movement disorders. He presented at age 11 years with a 4-year history of gradually worsening upper limb dystonia. Blood, urine, and CSF studies and a dystonia gene panel were unrevealing, and brain MRI showed nonspecific mild bilateral frontoparietal white matter changes.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) used parent-offspring trio whole-exome sequencing in the Family-2 proband and found the same heterozygous ATP5MC3 c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys) variant, which had arisen de novo. GeneMatcher had identified this match. The authors stated that this result confirmed the variant's pathogenicity for dystonia.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) screened 384 patients (362 with dystonia and 22 with hereditary spastic paraplegia) for variants in ATP5MC1, ATP5MC2, and ATP5MC3 and found no deleterious variants.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: In fibroblasts from the Family-1 proband (dystonia) and his affected father (HSP), Neilson et al. (2022) found normal activities of complexes I through IV. Complex V activity was reduced by 20%, cellular ATP by 20 to 32%, and oxygen consumption by 21 to 25%. Because oxygen consumption and ATP were reduced in proportion, the authors did not consider uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation a likely mechanism.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) noted that ATP5MC1 and ATP5MC2 also encode subunit c, so haploinsufficiency of ATP5MC3 would be unlikely to explain the severe phenotypes. They hypothesized that the mutant protein interferes with the F1-F0 interaction. They also suggested that differences in the relative expression of the mutant gene, for example between striatum and spinal cord, may account for the variable phenotype.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) overexpressed the Drosophila ATP5MC3 ortholog (CG1746) carrying either the human-equivalent p.N102K or the E. coli-equivalent p.N102E mutation under the arm-GAL4 driver. Both mutant lines climbed less well than wildtype in geotaxis assays, with p.N102K the slowest, whereas overexpression of wildtype protein had no effect. In fly mitochondria, complex V activity was reduced by 53% with p.N102K and by 37% with p.N102E.

subject: Neilson et al. (2022)
object: Neilson et al. (2022) reported that dystonia in Family-1 showed incomplete penetrance. Childhood-onset dystonia could generalize, and the spastic paraplegia began in adulthood and progressed gradually without other neurological problems.

subject: Zech et al. (2022)
object: Zech et al. (2022) described 3 unrelated patients with de novo heterozygous ATP5MC3 missense variants. Patient 8, a previously reported 12-year-old boy, had isolated upper-limb dystonia. Patient 9, a 15-year-old girl, had a history of milestone delay, pyramidal signs, and generalized dystonia with prominent upper-body involvement. Patient 10, a 6-year-old boy, had delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate.

subject: Zech et al. (2022)
object: In a 12-year-old boy with isolated upper-limb dystonia (patient 8), identified from a cohort of 1,012 dystonia patients with whole-exome sequencing, Zech et al. (2022) found a de novo heterozygous c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys) variant in ATP5MC3, the same variant previously identified in an independent pedigree with 18 of 40 members affected by dystonia and/or spasticity. The variant was absent from gnomAD and local control exomes. Patient fibroblasts showed a slight but significant decrease in ATPase activity and reduced oxygen consumption rate.

subject: Zech et al. (2022)
object: In a 15-year-old girl (patient 9) with milestone delay, pyramidal signs, and generalized dystonia, Zech et al. (2022) identified a de novo heterozygous c.319C>G (p.Pro107Ala) variant in ATP5MC3 by whole-exome sequencing. The variant was absent from gnomAD and local control exomes, affected a stringently conserved residue near the FO-F1 interaction loop, and was predicted deleterious by in silico tools.

subject: Zech et al. (2022)
object: In a 6-year-old boy (patient 10) with delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate, Zech et al. (2022) identified a de novo heterozygous c.236G>T (p.Gly79Val) variant in ATP5MC3, absent from gnomAD. Patient fibroblasts showed deficient ATPase activity and a moderate decrease in assembled ATPase on BN-PAGE; modeling placed Gly79 at an interhelical contact site possibly interfering with c-ring integrity.

subject: Zech et al. (2022)
object: Combining their 3 ATP5MC3 patients with the multigenerational family reported by Neilson et al., Zech et al. (2022) found that the ATP5MC3-associated condition included dystonia (12/18), spasticity/pyramidal signs (17/18), and developmental delay/intellectual disability (2/18). Dystonia-predominant syndromes were seen in 10 individuals; the authors noted that patients 9 and 10 confirmed spastic symptoms in independent families and introduced neurodevelopmental comorbidity.

subject: Zech et al. (2022)
object: Zech et al. (2022) found that ATP5MC3 c.236G>T, associated with a more severe neurodevelopmental disease-spasticity presentation, produced a significantly greater ATPase enzyme deficit than c.318C>G, associated with isolated dystonia, although they cautioned that further studies were required before genotype-phenotype correlations could be postulated.

subject: Zech et al. (2022)
object: Zech et al. (2022) suggested that dominant-negative effects could underlie disease caused by ATP5MC3 (and ATP5F1A) variants, supported by mild-to-moderate ATPase assembly and/or enzyme-activity defects in several patient cell lines.

subject: DYSTONIA, EARLY-ONSET, AND/OR SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA
